sections.decisionNote: Keep all five: each carries one wedge from facts.md (ONCE, NATIVE, AI, HONEST, STACK) that a homepage section can only tease. /why itself redirects to /why/components-run-once (no index page: the menu is the index).

pages.title: Components run once
pages.purpose: Your component runs once. Ever.

pages.title: One codebase
pages.purpose: One .tsx file. A website, an iPhone app and an Android app.

pages.title: AI-ready
pages.purpose: Your AI writes a bug. The framework catches it.

pages.title: Performance
pages.purpose: 2.6× faster than React. Don't trust us. Run it.

pages.title: Full stack
pages.purpose: SSG, SSR, ISR or SPA. Per route, in one line.

pages.title: Why Pyreon (redirect)
pages.purpose: Redirects to /why/components-run-once.
pages.reason: A five-item index adds a click and no content; the nav menu lists the five.

sections.decisionNote: Keep all six. /compare/react-native and the app-framework docs page (/docs/compare-app-frameworks) stay consistent: the compare page is the selling summary and links the docs page for Expo, Flutter, KMP and Capacitor.

pages.title: Pyreon vs React
pages.purpose: React ships 4× more JavaScript for the same app.

pages.title: Pyreon vs Next.js
pages.purpose: File routes, SSR, SSG and ISR. On components that run once.

pages.title: Pyreon vs Solid
pages.purpose: Same signals as Solid. `renderToString` up to 4.7× faster.

pages.title: Pyreon vs Vue
pages.purpose: Vue's reactivity without `.value`. In 1.6× less JavaScript.

pages.title: Pyreon vs Svelte
pages.purpose: 2,047 components. Mounted 3× faster than Svelte 5.

pages.title: Pyreon vs React Native and Expo
pages.purpose: One .tsx. A website, an iPhone app and an Android app.

pages.title: Compare (redirect)
pages.purpose: Redirects to /compare/react, the rival most visitors arrive with.
pages.reason: No index page; the menu lists the six.
